title: Moonglade Public Library — knowledge-bot field jot
body:
Context:
- Customer: Moonglade Public Library (regional library system, ~15 branches). Want a patron-facing chat assistant to answer catalog queries, branch hours, local events, and provide guided reference help. Must cite sources (catalog records, event pages, staff FAQ).
- Primary constraint: data residency + sensitive patron PII. They prefer Private (VPC) or on-prem; may accept Dedicated with strict KMS controls.
- Meeting 2026-03-09 w/ Head of Digital Services (L. Huang) + infra (T. Gomez).

Call notes (2026-03-09):
- Goal: replace phone/desk triage for common queries; pilot at 3 branches.
- Query mix: title/author search, availability, hold status, program schedules (events), directional questions, simple reference (e.g., how to request interlibrary loan).
- Expected traffic: 50 qps peak across three branches; average 2000 queries/day. Peak concurrent QPS likely short bursts during morning/evening.
- Latency tolerance: staff want <300ms token latency for short queries; acceptable up to 1s for complex retrievals.
- Security: data cannot leave their VPC; logs must be PII-scrubbed before leaving. KMS + HSM preferred for key management.
- Integration: their catalog is Evergreen ILS (Postgres-backed), events stored in a separate CMS (GraphQL API). They want live lookups for availability/holds.
- Staff tool: admin console + provenance viewer for staff to see which records used for answer.

Requirements (raw):
- Private deployment in their AWS account (VPC-mode).
- Retrieval pipeline that indexes: MARC-based catalog records, events, staff FAQs, branch pages. Should include versioning and re-index on nightly cadence; event updates must be near-real-time (webhook).
- Embedding refresh cadence: nightly for catalog delta; immediate for event webhook.
- Vector DB: they have an existing Postgres extension (pgvector) in-house; prefer using that over a new hosted DB.
- Model: start with a small open LLaMA-variant (7B quantized) for latency/cost; provide fallback to a 13B hosted model for complex QA or if hallucination thresholds exceeded.
- Observability: per-request token/time cost breakdown, route-level SLOs, provenance traces stored for 90 days.

Technical gotchas and notes: (scratch)
- Tokenization: MARC and long bibliographic fields need careful chunking — don't split ISBNs/author fields. Use metadata markers in chunks so retrieval can return fields for citation formatting.
- KV cache / prefix caching: many queries are short and repeated (branch hours, holidays). Suggest using prefix cache for branch/holiday prompts. Will reduce cost drastically.
- Streaming: patron UI prefers streaming short answers; but provenance needs to be attached — stream partial answer then append provenance block. Redwood streaming + trailing metadata support required.
- Real-time availability checks must be synchronous RPC to ILS. When ILS latency >200ms, degrade by returning cached availability with timestamp and an "updating" flag. Need circuit-breaker policy.
- PII: holds and patron names must be filtered from logs; build a redact pipeline in the agent that strips Patron IDs before sending to any external telemetry. Confirm that Private deployment keeps request/response in customer VPC until scrubbed.
- Embedding model drift: embeddings from different models may not be comparable. Keep embedding model pinned; store model id with each vector. If we need to migrate, plan reindex window and fallback.
- Fallback policy: if 7B model returns high hallucination score or cannot cite, forward to 13B (either hosted or customer-run) with attached retrieval context. Implement automatic A/B fallback threshold.

Architecture proposals (quick):
1) VPC Private: Redwood Private control plane + customer-deployed inference plane in their VPC. Use pgvector for storage + nightly batch reindex job in cluster. Webhook listener for events pushes incremental vectors.
2) Hybrid: Catalog queries go to on-prem pgvector; heavy LLM calls can route to Dedicated (hosted) 13B with encrypted transit only if KMS allows. Probably harder for compliance.

Short-term POC plan (4 weeks):
- Week 0: infra kickoff + right-sizing session (collect catalog size, avg record length, event volume). Ticket SE-4312 created.
- Week 1: index a 10k-sample of MARC records into pgvector; pipeline to convert MARC -> cleaned text + metadata (field tags).
- Week 2: spin up a Redwood Private node in Moonglade VPC (dev), deploy quantized 7B, integrate retrieval from sample pgvector, add availability RPC mock.
- Week 3: integrate streaming UI prototype, provenance attachments, run simulated load test (100 qps bursts), observe latency and costs.

Action items / Next steps (owners):
- Collect dataset sizes & sample exports (L. Huang) — due 2026-03-16.
- Infra checklist for VPC peering & KMS policy (T. Gomez) — due 2026-03-18.
- SE: create MARC->text extraction script + sample chunk rules (Maya) — 2026-03-12 (in progress). Jira: SE-4312.
- Dev: prototype pgvector ingest from sample dump (Noah) — 2026-03-19. GH: repo link in linked artifacts.
- UX: draft streaming + provenance flow for patron UI (Sofia) — 2026-03-20.

Open questions to clarify with customer:
- Are holds/availability considered "sensitive" PII at policy level? (affects logging)
- SLA expectations for availability/query during catalog maintenance windows
- Preferred cadence for embedding refresh for long-running metadata changes (e.g., renamed series)
- Acceptance criteria for hallucination thresholds (what fraction of answers can be non-citable before staff review?)

Random scratch reminders (for my impl notes):
- Add field markers like __TITLE__,__AUTHOR__,__MARC_650__ into chunks to help prompt templates pick fields.
- Consider using hybrid sparse retrieval (BM25) for exact-match title lookups to keep costs low; only call LLM for synth or explanation.
- Build safety prompt that says: "If you cannot find a citation in the corpus, respond: 'I don't have that information in the library catalog. Would you like help requesting it?'"

Status: still early; high customer interest for Private deployment. This doc = working scratchpad for POC.
